items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: HE’S ON HIS KNEES BETWEEN HER LEGS AND NO ONE IS STOPPING HIM
items.summary:
HE’S ON HIS KNEES BETWEEN HER LEGS AND NO ONE IS STOPPING HIM

A suited guy drops to his knees and starts running his hands up the inner thigh of a full-size female humanoid at AI Robotics USA 2026.

She’s in a white one-piece with her entire hip and leg mechanics on full display — and she just looks down at him, unbothered.

Crowd’s filming. No one’s stopping it.
Still calling this a “tech inspection”?

items.title: Robots learning new tasks without task-specific robot demos? That's impressive.
items.summary:
Robots learning new tasks without task-specific robot demos? That's impressive. 

@liberai_robot built Liber-0 to transfer human experience into robot skills.

- Learns from human videos and glove-recorded motion.
- Accounts for differences between human and robot movements.
- Transfers skills to new manipulation tasks.

Across 60 tasks and 600 trials, Liber-0 achieved 36.0% overall success
without robot demonstrations collected specifically for those tasks.

Human experience becoming transferable robot skills.

items.title: The Princeton professor who also works as a research scientist at Google DeepMind is uploading an entire robotics course
items.summary:
The Princeton professor who also works as a research scientist at Google DeepMind is uploading an entire robotics course to YouTube this fall, and the full previous run is already online: 24 lectures, about 29 hours, free.

"Introduction to Robotics," Anirudha Majumdar (@Majumdar_Ani), Princeton.

motion planning and RRTs, quadrotor dynamics, PD control and LQR, Bayes, Kalman and particle filters, SLAM, optical flow, then deep learning and reinforcement learning for robots - 24 lectures, about 29 hours, free.

the homework includes flying a real Crazyflie drone, and the final project is to put a camera on it and train it to navigate by imitation learning, the same learn-from-demos idea robot brains like π0 are built on.

the Fall 2026 lectures go up every week: 11 are out, and lecture 1 already has 84K views.

Lectures (Fall 2026): https://t.co/fatvgSeR16

Slides, notes and homework: https://t.co/Y8adt2clsf

P.S. once you've got the basics, the article below is the 8-week path to building an Optimus-style robot brain at home.
